findings.title: Call to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments does not compile
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160). A repository-wide search finds no zero-argument overload in `UsernamePasswordForm`, `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` or anywhere else, so the `services` module fails to compile. Pass the user: `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: `user != null` turns passkeys off on normal login and turns them on only for re-authentication
findings.body:
Before this change, the passkey (conditional UI) data was filled only when no user was set yet: in the `else` branch of `authenticate`, and under `context.getUser() == null` in `challenge`. The new helper requires `user != null`, so the condition is now the reverse:
- On a first login (`context.getUser()` is null), `authenticate` (line 115) no longer calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`. The username/password page then has no challenge and no `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`, so passwordless login through the default browser flow stops working.
- `challenge(...)` (line 137) drops passkeys after an unknown username, because `testInvalidUser` calls it with a null user (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:105-111).

The PR's own tests expect the passkey form on the first login page (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:196 and 238, `//form[@id='webauth']`), so they would fail.

The intended condition is probably `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && (user == null || user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType()))`. That keeps passkeys on the anonymous login page and shows them during re-authentication only to users who actually have a passkey.

findings.title: `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` turns passkeys off for the realm, so it never tests a user without a passkey
findings.body: The test sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so the passkey UI is hidden whatever credentials the user has. The comment at line 304 ("as this user does not have passkey") describes a case the test never reaches: passkeys enabled for the realm, re-authenticating a user who has only a password. That is the case the logic above gets wrong. Enable passkeys for the realm here and assert that `//form[@id='webauth']` is missing. Also, the `try { assertThat(..., nullValue()); fail(...) } catch (Exception)` pattern (lines 291-296 and 312-317) only works because `AssertionError` is not an `Exception`. `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`, as used in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest, states the intent directly.

contracts.action: UsernamePasswordForm fills the conditional-UI passkey data through isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code filled passkey data only in the user==null branch of authenticate and under context.getUser()==null in challenge
contracts.before_after: Before: passkeys on the anonymous login page, off during re-authentication. After: off on the anonymous login page (user==null), on during re-authentication.
contracts.visible_effect: The first login page loses the webauth form and the passkey prompt; the re-authentication page shows them.
contracts.failure_mode: Passwordless login through the default browser flow breaks for every realm with passkeys enabled.

contracts.action: UsernameForm skips the form on re-authentication only when passkeys are not enabled
contracts.before_after: Before: with a user set and no linked brokers, the form was skipped (success). After: falls through to UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate, which hides the username and shows the form.
contracts.visible_effect: The re-authenticating user sees a username page with the username hidden.
contracts.failure_mode: Does not compile (no zero-argument overload). Once fixed, users without a passkey get an extra page.

contracts.action: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator never sends allowed authenticators (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators=false), even when a user is set
contracts.equivalent_path: WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm 2FA branch, which lists the user's authenticators
contracts.before_after: During re-authentication the browser gets no allowCredentials list, so any discoverable key can respond. action() rejects a userHandle that does not match the user already set.
contracts.visible_effect: The passkey prompt is not limited to the current user's keys; a different user's key gives a WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER error.
contracts.failure_mode: A key belonging to a different user is rejected through setErrorResponse with DIFFERENT_USER_AUTHENTICATED.

contracts.action: Passkey error response and bad-password handler keep the re-authentication form attributes (username hidden, registration disabled)
contracts.before_after: Same attributes as the removed inline code; the auth note is set in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate when a user is already set.
contracts.visible_effect: After a failed attempt during re-authentication, the error page keeps the username hidden.

summary: The PR aims to allow passkey login during re-authentication (prompt=login), but as written it is broken. UsernameForm.java:47 calls a zero-argument `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` that does not exist, so the services module does not compile. The new helper in UsernamePasswordForm also uses `user != null`, the reverse of the old condition: passkeys disappear from the normal anonymous login page, which breaks passwordless login and the PR's own tests, and appear only during re-authentication. The helper also never checks whether the user has a passkey, so UsernameForm re-authentication now shows an extra page to users who have only a password. Moving the hide-username and disable-registration attributes into AuthenticatorUtils keeps the old behaviour, and a passkey of a different user is still rejected during re-authentication. The test meant to cover a user without a passkey turns passkeys off for the whole realm, so it does not cover that case.
